note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent judge, part-B backfill review) after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap}. RFC 7606 Section 8: 'A document that specifies a new BGP attribute MUST provide specifics regarding what constitutes an error for that attribute and how that error is to be handled.' The sentence binds the document, and its subject carries a relative clause that the not-applicable role binding cannot name, so the exclusion has no evidence the ratchet accepts and the summary records it as a gap. The earlier not-applicable verdict agreed with an annotation the owner has voided as authority (OR-1 note in the prior record, which flagged this row for re-derivation) and it is refused over a {gap} row. The behaviour Ze could be held to under the row is that each attribute it decodes is handled by the error rules its own document specifies; internal/component/bgp/message/rfc7606.go::validateAttribute is the per-attribute error dispatcher that would carry it, and no tagged unit asserts that every attribute it decodes follows its own document's error rules. With no test enforcing the row the verdict is unimplemented over that producer.
